notes:
Summary: Halcyon Bay runs a multi-tenant contact center SaaS used by retail and travel verticals. They're evaluating Redwood to replace a fragile in-house inference cluster that fails during seasonal peaks. Primary ask: predictable inference during incident bursts (Black Friday-like spikes) without creating noisy neighbor effects.

POC scope: agent-assist + ticket summarization + tool-calling (CRM API actions). Must support aggressive burst headroom: 5x baseline concurrent sessions for 30-60 minutes, with p95 response times that keep mean agent turn < 2s for assist suggestions and < 1s token latency for streaming insights.

Important quotes / customer color: "If the assist layer slows during our November peaks we lose SLAs and agents fall back to manual action — can't have that." — CTO.

Technical notes: interested in Dedicated pools + VPC private control plane. Wants automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants when capacity constrained, and routing by cost vs latency for non-critical summarization jobs. Need KMS/HSM proof-of-concept and audit log retention to 7 years for regulated clients.

POC success criteria (proposed):
- sustained 5x burst with < 5% error and no queue timeouts for 95% requests
- agent-assist suggestions delivered with median latency < 400ms and p95 < 900ms under burst
- ticket summarization throughput of 1200/hr with end-to-end accuracy within tolerance of current human baselines
- tool-calling reliability > 99.5% (idempotent call semantics tested)

Business drivers: reduce agent handle time, avoid seasonal overprovisioning costs, and bring observability into per-route cost + latency.

Engagement notes: AE (Jordan) is coordinating exec touchpoints. SE (Priya) to lead load plan and kernel selection discussion. CSM (Liam) likely to be included after contract.

Sticking points: legal residency, KMS schedule, and one outstanding Jira ticket about platform-level retry semantics.
pain_points:
- Unreliable inference during traffic spikes; incident backlog grows and human SLA breaches occur.
- Current infra requires 3x steady-state capacity to avoid saturation during promos.
- Tool-calls (CRM writes) fail intermittently under backpressure leading to duplicate tickets.
technical_requirements:
- VPC deployment with private control plane; optional on-prem connector for EU datacenters.
- KMS/HSM integration for encryption and key rotation.
- Per-route tracing and token-level cost breakdown available in console.
- Canary/circuit-breaker fallback: quantized model variant + lower-cost region routing.
- Autoscaling that respects latency SLOs and backpressure signals from queue length and agent presence.
commercial_notes: Looking for committed monthly capacity for peak months with burst pool for promos. Prefers annual contract with ramp. Budget in play across infra and platform line items. CFO wants clear unit economics and visible cost-savings compared to current cloud spend.
